# Integration and Release {.unnumbered}

\chapter*{Part III: Integration and Release}

Building an autonomous agent that operates successfully during a curated demonstration in a controlled laboratory is straightforward. Engineering a physical AI machine that can be safely released into the physical world alongside humans and critical infrastructure is an entirely different discipline.

When an autonomous system operates in production, three critical failure modes emerge:

1. **Resource Contention and Thermal Throttling:** When perception, world modeling, and trajectory generation run simultaneously, memory bus contention on unified memory architectures can cause tail latency spikes that trigger safety watchdog timeouts.
2. **Policy Endogeneity and Covariate Shift:** Fine-tuning learned models on operational logs that contain human safety interventions induces severe distributional collapse. The system inadvertently learns that dangerous states are normal, amplifying future errors.
3. **Unmodeled Physical Edge Cases:** Simulation benchmarks cannot prove that a system is safe against dirty camera lenses, dropped communication packets, microsecond clock skews, or sudden operating system kernel panics.

Part III shockproofs the complete physical AI system, establishes human-machine governance, and constructs the empirical safety case required for an accountable release verdict.


## The Integration, Assurance, and Frontier Spine

* **Chapter 10: Heterogeneous Compute Placement (Silicon Interconnects, Memory QoS, and Thermals):** We map the canonical pipeline stages across heterogeneous compute fabrics: cloud clusters, application processors, edge neural accelerators, and real-time microcontrollers. We budget memory footprints, allocate DMA channels, and configure bus QoS priorities to prevent vision streaming from starving motor packets.
* **Chapter 11: Runtime Governance and Safety Systems (Hazard Mitigation, Dual-Heartbeat Watchdogs, and Governed Flywheels):** We apply STPA hazard analysis, design dual-heartbeat hardware watchdogs, implement bumpless transfer filters that eliminate gearbox torque spikes during policy handoffs, and govern the telemetry flywheel without inducing policy endogeneity.
* **Chapter 12: Whole-System Verification, Assurance & Defensible Release (Hardware-in-the-Loop, Seeded Faults, and Deterministic Replay):** We establish deterministic flight-recorder replay logs, build HIL testbenches, subject the dual-brain agent to the live 4-fault seeded defense gauntlet, and construct the formal Claim-Argument-Evidence Defensible Release Case (REL-01).
* **Chapter 13: The Physical AI Frontier (Synthesis, Autonomous Fleets, and Society):** We synthesize the 12-chapter journey into the Physical AI Manifesto, exploring lifelong learning without safety regression, collective fleet intelligence, human-machine shared autonomy, and the ethical governance of software that moves mass.
